subject: Order Form: downstream productization & model-retrain carveouts
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <claire@tealpeak.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Markus Reinhardt <m.reinhardt@tealpeak.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — output ownership + training rights

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — TealPeak is excited about trying Redwood for our inference tier. Procurement has the draft Order Form attached and legal raised a couple of questions we need clarified before we can route to our CPO for signoff:

1) Output ownership: the draft MSA references a feedback license but the Order Form has a single-line note that looks like "Customer owns outputs". We need an explicit statement that TealPeak retains productization rights to outputs (including downstream code and product features derived from model outputs).

2) Training/use of customer data: procurement is insisting we get an explicit opt-out for any retraining of Redwood-hosted models with customer prompts/content — or, alternatively, we accept a narrow, anonymized usage for monitoring.

Could you confirm Redwood's standard position and whether the Order Form and MSA we received are aligned? I attached the draft Order Form as a PDF with the line items highlighted. Our procurement deadline is the 20th — any chance legal can review quickly?

Attachment: tealpeak_orderform_v1.pdf (PDF, 142KB)

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Dawson
Head of Procurement, TealPeak Analytics
claire@tealpeak.com | +1 415-555-0142


From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Claire Dawson <claire@tealpeak.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — output ownership + training rights

Claire — thanks for the clear note and the highlights. Short answers up front:

- Output ownership: Redwood's default MSA assigns customers rights to outputs for their productization; we try to avoid any blanket assignments back to Redwood. There are nuances for derivative models (we ask for narrow feedback licenses to improve service quality).
- Training/use: We can offer an explicit opt-out clause for model retraining at the customer level. Where customers opt-in to telemetry/feedback, we limit usage to aggregated, de-identified signals and provide controls.

I'm looping in Grace (product/legal) and Laura (contracts) to propose concrete redline language that we can add to the Order Form and MSA. Grace — can you propose two options (1: strict opt-out for retrain + customer owns outputs; 2: limited telemetry/feedback license for non-identifying monitoring) that we can push back to TealPeak with pros/cons? Procurement wants to hit the 20th.

Next step: I'll hold a 30-min sync tomorrow at 10am PT for redline review if that works for the legal team — LMK.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed redlines — outputs & training (two options)

Ben / Laura — below are two discrete draft clauses we can include in the Order Form (and mirror in the MSA exhibits). I kept them short so procurement/legal can drop them in and iterate.

OPTION A — Customer ownership, strict retrain opt-out
"Customer Outputs. Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to outputs generated by Customer’s use of the Service (\"Customer Outputs\"), including any derivative works, product features, or code derived from such outputs. Redwood shall not use Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any models or services without Customer’s prior written consent. Customer may elect to opt in or opt out of any telemetry-sharing program via the Order Form.

OPTION B — Customer ownership + limited feedback license (balanced)
"Customer Outputs. Customer retains ownership of Customer Outputs. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry derived from Customer’s use of the Service solely to monitor service health, detect abusive behavior, and improve infrastructure and models in a manner that does not allow Redwood to reconstruct Customer Input or Outputs or to create model weights specific to Customer data. This license does not permit training or fine-tuning of model weights on Customer Input or Outputs.

Notes:
- Pros/cons: A wins procurement quickly but prevents us from using signals to fix model regressions tied to a customer-specific use pattern. B gives Redwood minimal telemetry for diagnostics while keeping training locked down.
- For procurement asks, we should also include a one-sentence telemetry definition (what counts as \"de-identified, aggregated telemetry\"). I can draft that if legal wants.

I attached a docx with markup for both clauses and a short callout of rollback language if we need to escalate.

Attachment: proposed_redline_training_clause.docx (DOCX, 14KB)

Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Policy, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Claire Dawson <claire@tealpeak.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Markus Reinhardt <m.reinhardt@tealpeak.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — output ownership + training rights

Ben / Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround. TealPeak reviewed the two options with counsel; high-level feedback:

- We prefer OPTION A (strict opt-out) for procurement simplicity. Their concern is downstream productization — they need a clause that allows them to embed outputs into their product and sublicense within their standard commercial channels.
- If Redwood insists on any telemetry for model health, TealPeak wants hard guarantees: (i) no retention beyond 90 days for diagnostic telemetry, (ii) telemetry must be aggregated across at least 10 customers before it's usable for model improvement, and (iii) telemetry cannot contain any snippet of Customer Output or PII.

Markus also flagged that their procurement system requires a single-line confirmation in the Order Form that reads: "Customer shall retain all rights to Outputs and Redwood shall not use Customer Inputs or Outputs to train or improve models without explicit, opt-in consent." Can you confirm Redwood can add that sentence to the Order Form?

DocuSign path: https://docusign.com/TealPeak/Envelope/12345 (we'll wait until contract language is final).

Thanks,
Claire

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Exec sign-off requested: TealPeak — accept OPTION A with procurement carve-ins?

Marissa — quick ask for approval. TealPeak will only sign if we accept a strict opt-out for retraining and include the single-line confirmation in the Order Form. They also want the telemetry guarantees (90-day retention, min-10-customer aggregation, no PII/snippets).

Tradeoffs:
- Revenue impact: accepting OPTION A removes the ability to use TealPeak prompts/outputs for retraining, which reduces our customer-specific model improvement signals. However, TealPeak is a ~mid-sized opportunity (~$420k ARR) with fast time-to-close if we concede.
- Risk controls: We can accept their telemetry constraints but retain the right to use aggregated telemetry (min N customers) for infrastructure-only improvements. We should explicitly prohibit any reconstruction of inputs/outputs and exclude PII.

Recommended path (sales + product):
1) Agree to OPTION A in the Order Form and MSA (explicit opt-out for retrain).
2) Add the single-line confirmation TealPeak requested in the Order Form.
3) Log the telemetry constraints in the Order Form exhibit (90-day retention, min-10 aggregation, PII/snippet exclusion).

Marissa — do you approve this concession on commercial terms? If yes I’ll instruct Legal to prepare final redline and route DocuSign. If not, we push for OPTION B and provide a narrow carveout for monitoring only (will likely slow procurement).

Thanks,
Ben

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec sign-off requested: TealPeak — accept OPTION A with procurement carve-ins?

Ben / team — approved. Rationale: close the deal and retain a clear product treatment. We should accept OPTION A and add the procurement-friendly single-line confirmation in the Order Form. Also accept the telemetry guardrails as enumerated (90-day retention, min-10 aggregation, no PII/snippets).

Action items:

- Grace: draft the small definition paragraph for "de-identified, aggregated telemetry" and include the retention/aggregation thresholds.
- Ben: confirm to TealPeak that we'll send the redline by EOD and that DocuSign will be enabled once redline is agreed.
